claim: Midbrain dopamine neurons display heterogeneous properties even within a single neuroanatomical area.
source: Several studies have revealed that midbrain dopamine (DA) neurons, even within a single neuroanatomical area, display heterogeneous properties.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general finding from multiple studies, supported by citations throughout the introduction.

claim: Single-cell profiling techniques have begun to cluster DA neurons into subtypes based on their molecular signatures.
source: In parallel, studies using singlecell profiling techniques have begun to cluster DA neurons into subtypes based on their molecular signatures.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple citations in the introduction.

claim: Molecularly defined DA subtypes within the substantia nigra display distinctive anatomic and functional properties.
source: Recent work has shown that molecularly defined DA subtypes within the substantia nigra (SNc) display distinctive anatomic and functional properties, and differential vulnerability in Parkinson's disease (PD).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Molecularly defined DA subtypes within the substantia nigra display differential vulnerability in Parkinson's disease.
source: Recent work has shown that molecularly defined DA subtypes within the substantia nigra (SNc) display distinctive anatomic and functional properties, and differential vulnerability in Parkinson's disease (PD).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: The study generated a high-resolution hierarchically organized map revealing 20 molecularly distinct DA neuron subtypes belonging to three main families.
source: We developed an optimized pipeline for single-nuclear RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) and generated a high-resolution hierarchically organized map revealing 20 molecularly distinct DA neuron subtypes belonging to three main families.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through the results section with clustering analysis.

claim: The study mapped the location of DA neuron subtypes in the mouse midbrain using MERFISH technology.
source: We integrated this data with spatial MERFISH technology to map, with high definition, the location of these subtypes in the mouse midbrain, revealing heterogeneity even within neuroanatomical sub-structures.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through MERFISH results.

claim: Heterogeneity exists even within neuroanatomical sub-structures of the midbrain.
source: We integrated this data with spatial MERFISH technology to map, with high definition, the location of these subtypes in the mouse midbrain, revealing heterogeneity even within neuroanatomical sub-structures.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through spatial mapping results.

claim: In the LRRK2G2019S knock-in mouse model of PD, DA subtype organization and proportions are preserved.
source: Finally, we demonstrate that in the preclinical LRRK2G2019S knock-in mouse model of PD, subtype organization and proportions are preserved.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through comparative analysis of control and mutant samples.

claim: Transcriptional alterations occur in many DA subtypes in the LRRK2G2019S model, including those localized to the ventral tier SNc.
source: Transcriptional alterations occur in many subtypes including those localized to the ventral tier SNc, where differential expression is observed in synaptic pathways, which might account for previously described DA release deficits in this model.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through differential expression analysis.

claim: Differential expression in synaptic pathways in ventral tier SNc neurons might account for previously described DA release deficits in the LRRK2G2019S model.
source: Transcriptional alterations occur in many subtypes including those localized to the ventral tier SNc, where differential expression is observed in synaptic pathways, which might account for previously described DA release deficits in this model.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data connecting observed transcriptional changes to previously reported phenotypes.

claim: Midbrain DA neurons are traditionally organized in three main anatomical areas: the ventral tegmental area (VTA), SNc, and retrorubral area (RR).
source: Midbrain DA neurons are traditionally organized in three main anatomical areas – the ventral tegmental area (VTA), SNc, and retrorubral area (RR) (Björklund and Dunnett, 2007), with further sub-divisions therein (Fu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: Recent studies have revealed diversity within clusters of DA neurons in electrophysiological properties and responses during various behavioral paradigms.
source: Recent studies have indeed revealed diversity within clusters in electrophysiological properties as well as responses during various behavioral paradigms (Evans et al., 2017; Menegas et al., 2018; Engelhard et al., 2019; Lammel et al., 2008; da Silva et al., 2018; Matsumoto and Hikosaka, 2009; Beier et al., 2015; Avvisati et al., 2024; Brischoux et al., 2009; Heymann et al., 2020; Howe and Dombeck, 2016; Lerner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations from prior literature.

claim: In the SNc, activity in a ventral Anxa1+ population is correlated to acceleration in mice on a treadmill.
source: For example, in the SNc, activity in a ventral Anxa1 + population is correlated to acceleration in mice on a treadmill, whereas activity in dorsal Calb1 + or lateral Vglut2 + populations is correlated to deceleration (Azcorra et al., 2023).
evidence: This is cited from a prior study.

claim: Activity in dorsal Calb1+ or lateral Vglut2+ populations in the SNc is correlated to deceleration in mice on a treadmill.
source: For example, in the SNc, activity in a ventral Anxa1 + population is correlated to acceleration in mice on a treadmill, whereas activity in dorsal Calb1 + or lateral Vglut2 + populations is correlated to deceleration (Azcorra et al., 2023).
evidence: This is cited from a prior study.

claim: Previous studies using single-cell sequencing in mice have been limited by the number of cells analyzed, the quality of cDNA library, and bias during isolation.
source: Previous studies using single-cell sequencing in mice have been limited by the number of cells analyzed, the quality of cDNA library, as well as bias during isolation, thus providing an incomplete picture of DA neuron subtypes (Poulin et al., 2020; La Manno et al., 2016; Kramer et al., 2018; Hook et al., 2018; Tiklová et al., 2019; Saunders et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an assessment of prior literature with citations.

claim: Pathogenic mutations which increase leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) activity are one of the most common causes of autosomal dominant PD.
source: Pathogenic mutations which increase leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) activity are one of the most common causes of autosomal dominant PD and clinically similar to sporadic cases (Greggio et al., 2006; Tokars et al., 2022; Taymans et al., 2023).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: LRRK2-related PD is clinically similar to sporadic cases.
source: Pathogenic mutations which increase leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) activity are one of the most common causes of autosomal dominant PD and clinically similar to sporadic cases (Greggio et al., 2006; Tokars et al., 2022; Taymans et al., 2023).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: In patients with idiopathic PD, LRRK2 kinase activity is increased in DA neurons.
source: Additionally, even in patients with idiopathic PD, LRRK2 kinase activity is increased in DA neurons (Di Maio et al., 2018), providing justification for studying LRRK2-driven mechanisms in DA neurons.
evidence: This is cited from prior literature.

claim: Structural and functional synaptic changes are a recurring theme with LRRK2 mutations.
source: Structural and functional synaptic changes are a recurring theme with LRRK2 mutations (Khan et al., 2024; Matikainen-Ankney et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations from prior literature.

claim: Impaired DA transmission is observed with several LRRK2 mouse models including knock-in mouse lines expressing the G2019S mutation at physiological levels.
source: Accordingly, impaired DA transmission is observed with several LRRK2 mouse models including knock-in (KI) mouse lines expressing the most common LRRK2 mutation (G2019S) at physiological levels (Xenias et al., 2022; Yue et al., 2015; Tozzi et al., 2018), suggestive of functional synaptic deficits in dopaminergic circuits in the absence of overt DA neuron loss.
evidence: This is cited from prior literature.

claim: LRRK2 KI mouse models show functional synaptic deficits in dopaminergic circuits in the absence of overt DA neuron loss.
source: Accordingly, impaired DA transmission is observed with several LRRK2 mouse models including knock-in (KI) mouse lines expressing the most common LRRK2 mutation (G2019S) at physiological levels (Xenias et al., 2022; Yue et al., 2015; Tozzi et al., 2018), suggestive of functional synaptic deficits in dopaminergic circuits in the absence of overt DA neuron loss.
evidence: This is an interpretation of cited findings from prior literature.

claim: The study profiled 28,532 cells after quality control filtering with a median UMI count of 7750.5 and median of 3056 genes.
source: This improved protocol enabled increased yield and sample quality (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A). Doing so enabled us to generate a dataset with 28,532 profiled cells (after quality control filtering) with a median UMI count of 7750.5 and median of 3056 genes.
evidence: This is a direct report of the dataset characteristics.

claim: Downstream clustering resulted in 22 unique clusters, of which two clusters (16 and 21, 911 total cells) were determined to represent possible dopaminergic/glial doublets.
source: Downstream clustering resulted in 22 unique clusters (Figure 1B), of which two clusters (16 and 21, 911 total cells) were determined to represent possible dopaminergic/glial doublets based on co-expression of glial markers in these populations and were excluded from downstream analyses (shown in gray in Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a direct report of the clustering results with reasoning for exclusion.

claim: The 20 remaining clusters all showed expression of key pan-dopaminergic markers including Slc18a2 (Vmat2), Ddc, Th, and Slc6a3 (Dat).
source: The 20 remaining clusters all showed expression of key pan-dopaminergic markers including Slc18a2 (Vmat2), Ddc, Th, and Slc6a3 (Dat) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The identified subtypes were observed in both males and females, and across genotypes, in similar proportions.
source: These clusters were observed in both males and females, and across genotypes, in similar proportions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The increased yield and sample quality allowed explicit detection of known populations that have eluded most prior single-cell studies, such as DA neurons expressing Vip.
source: However, our increased yield and sample quality also allowed explicit detection of known populations that have eluded most prior single-cell studies, such as DA neurons expressing Vip (Poulin et al., 2020; Poulin et al., 2014), thereby demonstrating the strength of this pipeline in detecting rare DA neuron subtypes.
evidence: This is stated as a finding with citations to prior work that identified these populations.

claim: All the described subtypes showed high expression of midbrain floorplate markers, with exception of clusters 0 and 17.
source: Importantly, all the described subtypes showed high expression of midbrain floorplate markers (Figure 1E), with exception of clusters 0 and 17, which possibly represent Slc6a3+ neurons in the supramammillary and/or premamillary regions (Soden et al., 2016; Nouri and Awatramani, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Clusters 0 and 17 possibly represent Slc6a3+ neurons in the supramammillary and/or premamillary regions.
source: Importantly, all the described subtypes showed high expression of midbrain floorplate markers (Figure 1E), with exception of clusters 0 and 17, which possibly represent Slc6a3+ neurons in the supramammillary and/or premamillary regions (Soden et al., 2016; Nouri and Awatramani, 2017).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the lack of floorplate markers and citations to prior work.

claim: The earliest division point among the clusters was defined by genes Prkcd and Lef1, which are highly expressed only in cluster 17.
source: The earliest division point among our clusters was defined by genes Prkcd and Lef1, which are highly expressed only in cluster 17 (Log2 fold changes = 6.279 and 7.246 respectively, BH-corrected p-values ≈ 0; note, such p-values are calculated using default Seurat differential expression functions which treat each cell as an independent sample thus potentially inflating statistical significance).
evidence: This is a direct report of differential expression analysis results.

claim: A family of clusters defined by Gad2/Kctd16 separated from all other clusters, which expressed significantly higher levels of Ddc and Slc6a3.
source: Next, a family of clusters defined by Gad2/Kctd16 (deemed Gad2 family, Log2 fold changes = 5.318 and 4.014 respectively, BH-corrected p-values ≈ 0) separated from all other clusters, which expressed significantly higher levels of Ddc and Slc6a3 (Log2 fold changes = 1.419 and 1.643 respectively, BH-corrected p-values ≈ 0).
evidence: This is a direct report of differential expression analysis results.

claim: The first major branch point between Ddc-high/Slc6a3-high clusters was defined by cells expressing Sox6/Col25a1 versus those expressing Calb1/Ndst3.
source: The first major branch point between Ddc-high/Slc6a3-high clusters was then defined by cells expressing Sox6/Col25a1 (Log2 fold changes = 2.720 and 2.305 respectively, BH-corrected p-values ≈ 0) versus those expressing Calb1/Ndst3 (Log2 fold changes = 2.025 and 3.368 respectively, BH-corrected p-values ≈ 0), thus creating the Sox6 family and Calb1 families, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct report of differential expression analysis results.

claim: The division between Sox6 and Calb1 is consistent with a prior large single-cell profiling study that found this division to be the central branch point among DA neurons across several species including humans.
source: This division between Sox6 and Calb1 is consistent with our previous work (Poulin et al., 2014), as well as a prior large single-cell profiling study that found this division to be the central branch point among DA neurons across several species including humans (Kamath et al., 2022; Siletti et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior literature with citations.

claim: The Sox6 family is split into two branches with six subtypes.
source: The Sox6 family is split into two branches with six subtypes, the Calb1 family is split into two branches with ten subtypes, whereas the Gad2 family can be further split into two subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct report of the clustering structure.

claim: The Calb1 family is split into two branches with ten subtypes.
source: The Sox6 family is split into two branches with six subtypes, the Calb1 family is split into two branches with ten subtypes, whereas the Gad2 family can be further split into two subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct report of the clustering structure.

claim: The Gad2 family can be further split into two subtypes.
source: The Sox6 family is split into two branches with six subtypes, the Calb1 family is split into two branches with ten subtypes, whereas the Gad2 family can be further split into two subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct report of the clustering structure.

claim: A population of DA neurons was identified among the 40 MERFISH clusters based on the expression of Th, Slc6a3, and Slc18a2.
source: A population of DA neurons was identified among our 40 clusters based on the expression Th, Slc6a3, and Slc18a2 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The DA neuron cluster comprised 4532 cells and was entirely located in the midbrain.
source: This cluster comprised 4532 cells, was entirely located in the midbrain, and was also enriched for Ddc, Dlk1, and Drd2 (not shown).
evidence: This is a direct report of the MERFISH clustering results.

claim: Within the DA population, expression of genes associated with glutamatergic and GABAergic neurotransmission was detected, in line with previous reports of multi-lingual characteristics of DA neurons.
source: Within this population, we detected expression of genes associated with glutamatergic and GABAergic neurotransmission, in line with previous reports of multi-lingual characteristics of DA neurons (Trudeau et al., 2014; Descarries et al., 2008; Morales and Root, 2014; Morales and Margolis, 2017; Tritsch et al., 2016; Conrad et al., 2024), for instance, the glutamatergic marker Slc17a6 (Vglut2) and GABAergic markers Gad2 and Slc32a1 (Vgat) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations and shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Cells in the DA neuron cluster were located in the following locations: 35.2% in the SNc, 19.8% in the VTA, 7.8% in the CLi, 15.3% in the RR, 2.0% in the IF, 0.6% in the RLi, 4% in the PAG and 15.3% located elsewhere.
source: We found that cells in our DA neuron cluster were located in the following locations: 35.2% in the SNc, 19.8% in the VTA, 7.8% in the CLi, 15.3% in the RR, 2.0% in the IF, 0.6% in the RLi, 4% in the PAG and 15.3% located elsewhere (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a direct report of the spatial distribution analysis.

claim: Subclustering of the 4532 DA cells identified by MERFISH resolved 12 distinct subgroups.
source: Finally, to explore the diversity of DA neurons identified by MERFISH, we subclustered the 4532 cells to resolve 12 distinct subgroups (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C–F).
evidence: This is a direct report of the subclustering analysis.

claim: The study successfully projected the MERFISH dataset onto the snRNA-seq UMAP space and selected 2297 dopamine neurons with a cell similarity score >0.5.
source: We successfully projected the MERFISH dataset onto the snRNA-seq UMAP space and selected for 2297 dopamine neurons with a cell similarity score >0.5 (mean value, 0.538), increasing confidence in the correct assignment to snRNA-seq defined clusters.
evidence: This is a direct report of the data integration results.

claim: Almost all clusters were represented by more than 20 cells in the MERFISH dataset.
source: Almost all clusters were represented by more than 20 cells in our MERFISH dataset (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in figures.

claim: Clusters Calb1Ccdc192 and Calb1Gipr were not resolved in the label transfer either due to their relatively smaller number or location in an under-sampled region.
source: Clusters Calb1Ccdc192 and Calb1Gipr were not resolved in this label transfer either due to their relatively smaller number or location in an under-sampled region.
evidence: This is an interpretation of why certain clusters were not detected in the MERFISH data.

claim: The Vip-expressing Calb1Gipr has been shown to be located in the caudal midbrain (PAG/DR).
source: Indeed, the Vip-expressing Calb1Gipr has been shown to be located in the caudal midbrain (PAG/DR) (Poulin et al., 2014), a region not well covered in our MERFISH experiment.
evidence: This is cited from prior literature.

claim: Half of the snRNA-seq clusters were predominantly comprised of single MERFISH clusters (10/20) and 25% (5/20) were comprised of two MERFISH clusters.
source: Half of the snRNA-seq clusters were predominantly comprised of single MERFISH clusters (10/20) and 25% (5/20) were comprised of two MERFISH clusters, demonstrating that the integration with the snRNA-seq dataset allowed us to further refine our MERFISH-based classification (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct report of the comparison between clustering methods.

claim: The imputed data across the genes used for data integration correlated strongly with MERFISH transcripts, particularly for Calb1, Gad2, and Aldh1a1 genes.
source: The imputed data across the genes used for data integration correlated strongly with MERFISH transcripts, particularly for Calb1, Gad2, and Aldh1a1 genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The SNc is composed of 78.4% of neurons from the Sox6 family.
source: Each family was overrepresented in a neuroanatomically-defined area; for instance, the SNc is composed of 78.4% of neurons from the Sox6 family (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), consistent with previous reports (Pereira Luppi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a direct report of the spatial distribution analysis with citation to prior work.

claim: Each DA neuron family was found across multiple neuroanatomical regions.
source: However, each family was also found across multiple neuroanatomical regions (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in supplementary figures.

claim: One branch of the Calb1 family (defined by higher Lepr expression) was enriched in the dorsal VTA.
source: For example, one branch of the Calb1 family dendrogram (Figure 4, label in shades of yellow-orange defined by higher Lepr expression) was enriched in the dorsal VTA, whereas the other Calb1 branch (Figure 4, label in shades of red defined by higher Ntm expression) populated mostly the ventromedial VTA.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4.

claim: The other branch of the Calb1 family (defined by higher Ntm expression) populated mostly the ventromedial VTA.
source: For example, one branch of the Calb1 family dendrogram (Figure 4, label in shades of yellow-orange defined by higher Lepr expression) was enriched in the dorsal VTA, whereas the other Calb1 branch (Figure 4, label in shades of red defined by higher Ntm expression) populated mostly the ventromedial VTA.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Branch 1 of the Sox6 family is located more dorsal and medial than Branch 2.
source: We observed an important discrepancy between these two branches, with Branch 1 being located more dorsal and medial than Branch 2 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In the caudal SNc and RR, neurons from both branches of the Sox6 family are mostly intermixed.
source: Interestingly, this dorsoventral organization breaks down in the caudal SNc and RR where neurons from both branches are mostly intermixed.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the spatial mapping data.

claim: Within Branch 2 of the Sox6 family, neurons of cluster Sox6Arhgap28 were found to be more lateral in the SNc compared to neurons of Sox6Tafa1, Sox6Kcnmb2, or Sox6Vcan.
source: Within Branch 2, the molecular identity correlated with the medio-lateral distribution. For instance, neurons of cluster Sox6Arhgap28 were found to be more lateral in the SNc compared to neurons of Sox6Tafa1, Sox6Kcnmb2, or Sox6Vcan.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the spatial mapping data.

claim: The medio-lateral distribution of neurons of the SNc ventral tier might reflect the differential topographical distribution of nigrostriatal projections previously reported.
source: This medio-lateral distribution of neurons of the SNc ventral tier might reflect the differential topographical distribution of nigrostriatal projections previously reported (Wu et al., 2019; Poulin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the observed spatial distribution to prior findings.

claim: Branch 1 Calb1 neurons tended to localize to the dorsal VTA while Branch 2 Calb1 neurons showed distinct ventromedial localization.
source: Within the VTA, Branch 1 Calb1 neurons tended to localize to the dorsal VTA (Figure 6A–B) while Branch 2 Calb1 neurons showed distinct ventromedial localization (Figure 6C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6.

claim: Subtypes Calb1Ptprt and Calb1Sox6 were largely absent from the SNc dorsal tier and RR, whereas subtype Calb1Sulf1 was present.
source: Within Branch 1, subtypes Calb1Ptprt and Calb1Sox6 were largely absent from the SNc dorsal tier and RR, whereas subtype Calb1Sulf1 was present.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the spatial mapping data.

claim: Subtypes Calb1Sulf1 and Calb1Lpar1 were each observed in significant numbers in the dorsolateral SNc/SNpl region.
source: Some notable distinctions were observed in both groups, specifically subtypes Calb1Sulf1 and Calb1Lpar1 which were each observed in significant numbers in the dorsolateral SNc/SNpl region.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the spatial mapping data.

claim: Calb1Lpar1 is a likely candidate for the SNpl Vglut2+ DA neuron population found to innervate the tail of the striatum.
source: Of these, only Calb1Lpar1 expressed significant Slc17a6 (data not shown), making it a likely candidate for the SNpl Vglut2 + DA neuron population found to innervate the tail of the striatum (Poulin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression and citation to prior work.

claim: Laterally located DA neurons have been genetically targeted with a Slc17a6-Cre driver, and display deceleration-correlated responses, and robust responses to physically aversive stimuli.
source: Indeed, these laterally located neurons have been genetically targeted with a Slc17a6-Cre driver, and display deceleration-correlated responses, and robust responses to physically aversive stimuli (Azcorra et al., 2023; Poulin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature.

claim: Subtypes Gad2Egfr and Gad2Ebf2 had very similar spatial distributions and were prominent in the posterior IF, RLi, and CLi.
source: Subtypes Gad2Egfr and Gad2Ebf2 had very similar spatial distributions and were prominent in the posterior IF, RLi, and CLi (Figure 7, Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in figures.

claim: All Gad2 subtypes expressed Slc32a1, opening the possibility that these neurons co-release GABA.
source: All Gad2 subtypes expressed Slc32a1, opening the possibility that these neurons co-release GABA.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with speculation about functional implications.

claim: Gad2 subtypes also expressed Slc17a6, revealing potentially multilingual DA neuron subtypes.
source: Further, they also expressed Slc17a6, revealing potentially multilingual DA neuron subtypes.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with speculation about functional implications.

claim: Lrrk2 expression is detectable across most DA neuron subtypes, with the notable exception of Gad2Egfr neurons.
source: We found detectable expression across most subtypes, with the notable exception of Gad2Egfr neurons.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the expression analysis shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The relative proportions of each DA subtype within the dataset are relatively unchanged between control and LRRK2G2019S mutant samples.
source: We first graphed the proportions of each subtype within our control and mutant datasets (Figure 8B), and found remarkable similarity across these samples, consistent with previous reports showing no DA neuron loss in these mice (Yue et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 8B with citation to prior work.

claim: MetaNeighbor analysis revealed that the most similar population to each wildtype cluster was its corresponding subtype in the Lrrk2 mutant samples.
source: MetaNeighbor analysis revealed that the most similar population to each wildtype cluster was its corresponding subtype in the Lrrk2 mutant samples.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the MetaNeighbor analysis shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The general subtype organization is largely impervious to LRRK2G2019S perturbation.
source: This suggests that the general subtype organization is largely impervious to LRRK2G2019S perturbation, and that our clustering scheme is likely more reflective of cell type rather than cell state.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the MetaNeighbor results.

claim: The clustering scheme is likely more reflective of cell type rather than cell state.
source: This suggests that the general subtype organization is largely impervious to LRRK2G2019S perturbation, and that our clustering scheme is likely more reflective of cell type rather than cell state.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the MetaNeighbor results.

claim: Calculating differentially expressed genes across all clusters revealed 1646 genes in total with BH corrected p-value <0.05 between LRRK2G2019S mutants and controls.
source: Calculating differentially expressed genes across all clusters revealed a large number of significantly enriched or diminished genes as a function of Lrrk2 mutation (1646 genes in total with BH corrected p-value <0.05, Wilcoxon rank sum test).
evidence: This is a direct report of the differential expression analysis results.

claim: Most gene expression changes in LRRK2G2019S mutants appear to be small in magnitude.
source: Notably, most of these changes appear to be small in magnitude; among FDR-significant genes, only 51 showed increased expression and seven showed decreased expression with log2 fold changes greater than 0.5 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the differential expression analysis.

claim: AC149090.1 is orthologous to the human PISD gene, which is involved in autophagy and implicated in mitochondrial dysfunction.
source: AC149090.1 is orthologous to the human PISD gene, which is involved in autophagy and implicated in mitochondrial dysfunction (Buckley et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2019; Thomas et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: AC149090.1 has been proposed as a sensitive marker of biological aging in the brain.
source: This gene has been proposed as a sensitive marker of biological aging in the brain (Buckley et al., 2023; Jin et al., 2023), an interesting finding given that age is the single largest risk factor for PD.
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: Mir124a-1hg is a host gene for miR-124, a microRNA with purported neuroprotective effects that has been found to be downregulated in PD patients or some PD mouse models.
source: Also of note, Mir124a-1hg is a host gene (though not the exclusive gene) for miR-124, a microRNA with purported neuroprotective effects that has been found to be downregulated in PD patients or some PD mouse models (Zhang et al., 2022b; Yao et al., 2018; Han et al., 2019; Angelopoulou et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: Using GSEA, 18 gene sets with significant differential expression (FDR-adjusted p-values <0.05) were found between LRRK2G2019S mutants and controls.
source: Using GSEA, we found 18 gene sets with significant differential expression (FDR-adjustedp-values <0.05).
evidence: This is a direct report of the GSEA results.

claim: Many of the top enriched pathways in LRRK2G2019S mutants were related to energy production via mitochondrial oxidative respiration.
source: While a broad range of biological domains are found among these results, many of the top enriched pathways were related to energy production via mitochondrial oxidative respiration, remarkably similar to prior comparisons between vulnerable and resistant DA neuron populations (Pereira Luppi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the GSEA results with citation to prior work.

claim: Mitochondrial energy production pathways and the extraordinary bioenergetic burdens of DA neurons have been heavily implicated in PD vulnerability.
source: Mitochondrial energy production pathways, and specifically the extraordinary bioenergetic burdens of DA neurons, have been heavily implicated in PD vulnerability (González-Rodríguez et al., 2021; Surmeier et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: Using GO, the top pathways displaying significant differential expression between Lrrk2 mutants and controls are all associated with synaptic organization and functions.
source: Utilizing GO, we again found many pathways displaying significant differential expression between Lrrk2 mutants and controls. Among these, the top pathways are all associated with synaptic organization and functions (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 8E.

claim: Pre-synaptic dysfunction in Lrrk2 mutants such as endocytosis or axonal cargo trafficking impairments could underpin the deficits in DA signaling observed in these mice.
source: This was particularly intriguing given that pre-synaptic dysfunction in Lrrk2 mutants such as endocytosis (Nguyen and Krainc, 2018; Soukup et al., 2016; Islam et al., 2016) or axonal cargo trafficking impairments (Boecker et al., 2021) could underpin the deficits in DA signaling observed in these mice (Skelton et al., 2022; Pischedda and Piccoli, 2021).
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the observed pathway enrichment to prior findings.

claim: Decreased endocytosis has been observed in DA neurons but not cortical or hippocampal LRRK2G2019S primary neurons.
source: Of note, decreased endocytosis has been observed in DA neurons but not cortical or hippocampal LRRK2G2019S primary neurons (Pan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature.

claim: Cell type-specific synaptic effects on DA neurons are consistent with their vulnerability in LRRK2-related PD.
source: These results, although in vitro, suggest cell type-specific synaptic effects on DA neurons, consistent with their vulnerability in LRRK2-related PD.
evidence: This is an interpretation of cited findings.

claim: 729 DEGs were found among the Sox6 family and 679 among the Calb1 family when comparing LRRK2G2019S mutants versus control mice.
source: We found 729 DEGs among the Sox6 family, and 679 among the Calb1 family (BH corrected p-value <0.05).
evidence: This is a direct report of the differential expression analysis results.

claim: 327 DEGs were shared between the Sox6 and Calb1 families.
source: Among those genes, we found 327 DEGs were shared between the Sox6 and Calb1 families (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in supplementary figures.

claim: AC149090.1 was highly significant in both Sox6 and Calb1 cohorts, implying that the pan-DA differential expression of this gene was not driven by a particular subset of DA neurons.
source: Notably, AC149090.1 was highly significant in both cohorts, implying that the pan-DA differential expression of this gene was not driven by a particular subset of DA neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differential expression results.

claim: GO revealed pathways that largely corresponded to synaptic and axonal function, but with higher significance of results in the Sox6 family than in Calb1 or Gad2 families.
source: In line with our previous results, GO revealed pathways that largely corresponded to synaptic and axonal function, but with higher significance of results in the Sox6 family than in Calb1 or Gad2 families (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Within the Sox6 family, GSEA analysis showed an upregulation of energy production and metabolism pathways and a downregulation of intercellular communication pathways.
source: Within the Sox6 family, GSEA analysis showed an upregulation of energy production and metabolism pathways similar to those observed at the global level, as well as a downregulation of intercellular communication pathways (Figure 9B, top five upregulated and downregulated pathways shown for each family).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The Sox6Tafa1 SNc subtype was of particular interest given recent results showing that Anxa1+ ventral tier SNc neuronal activity is selectively correlated with acceleration in mice running on a treadmill.
source: The Sox6Tafa1 SNc subtype was of particular interest to us given recent results showing that Anxa1 + ventral tier SNc neuronal activity is selectively correlated with acceleration in mice running on a treadmill, leading to the hypothesis that degeneration of these neurons may contribute to motor deficits seen in PD (Azcorra et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with citation to prior work.

claim: Degeneration of Anxa1+ ventral tier SNc neurons may contribute to motor deficits seen in PD.
source: The Sox6Tafa1 SNc subtype was of particular interest to us given recent results showing that Anxa1 + ventral tier SNc neuronal activity is selectively correlated with acceleration in mice running on a treadmill, leading to the hypothesis that degeneration of these neurons may contribute to motor deficits seen in PD (Azcorra et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on cited prior work.

claim: Similar pathways were observed in Sox6Tafa1 and Calb1Stac subtypes, however with substantially higher significance values observed in the Sox6Tafa1 cluster.
source: Similar pathways were observed in each subtype, including several pathways once again corresponding to synaptic function, however with substantially higher significance values observed in the Sox6Tafa1 cluster.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the GO analysis.

claim: Of the DEGs in the Sox6 family, Calb1 family, and Sox6Tafa1 cluster, 24.82%, 20.19%, and 29.41% of these genes had synaptic localizations, respectively.
source: Of the DEGs in the Sox6 family, Calb1 family, and Sox6Tafa1 cluster, 24.82%, 20.19%, and 29.41% of these genes had synaptic localizations, respectively, with more significant synaptic associations among populations localized to ventral tier SNc (Figure 9C, Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct report of the SynGO analysis results.

claim: Among synaptic DEGs annotated by SynGO, 45.83% of Sox6 family, 64.0% of Sox6Tafa1, and 48.82% of Calb1 family DEGs have presynaptic localizations.
source: Further compartment categorization revealed that among these synaptic DEGs annotated by SynGO, 45.83% of Sox6 family (11.38% of total DEGs), 64.0% of Sox6Tafa1 (18.82% of total DEGs) and 48.82% of Calb1 family (9.86% of total DEGs) DEGs have presynaptic localizations, raising the possibility of enhanced disruption of presynaptic function in acceleration-correlated DA neurons.
evidence: This is a direct report of the SynGO analysis results with interpretation.

claim: There is a possibility of enhanced disruption of presynaptic function in acceleration-correlated DA neurons.
source: Further compartment categorization revealed that among these synaptic DEGs annotated by SynGO, 45.83% of Sox6 family (11.38% of total DEGs), 64.0% of Sox6Tafa1 (18.82% of total DEGs) and 48.82% of Calb1 family (9.86% of total DEGs) DEGs have presynaptic localizations, raising the possibility of enhanced disruption of presynaptic function in acceleration-correlated DA neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the SynGO analysis results.

claim: Greater proportions of DEGs are associated with presynaptic locations in cells from vulnerable DA neurons (Sox6 family, and in particular, Sox6Tafa1), compared to less vulnerable ones (Calb1 family).
source: Overall, greater proportions of DEGs are associated with presynaptic locations in cells from vulnerable DA neurons (Sox6 family, and in particular, Sox6Tafa1), compared to less vulnerable ones (Calb1 family).
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the SynGO analysis results.

claim: scDRS analysis revealed clear bias for higher PD GWAS risk scores among clusters that localize to the ventral SNc.
source: We first calculated a PD GWAS risk score for each individual cell, which revealed clear bias for higher risk scores among clusters that localize to the ventral SNc (Figure 9F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9F.

claim: Significant PD risk associations were confirmed in several clusters, particularly those in the Sox6 family.
source: We confirmed significant risk associations in several clusters, particularly those in the Sox6 family (Figure 9G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9G.

claim: The Gad2 family of clusters all showed significant negative associations with PD risk loci.
source: Interestingly, the Gad2 family of clusters all showed significant negative associations with PD risk loci (Figure 9G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9G.

claim: The highest scDRS scores were in clusters Sox6Tafa1 and Sox6Vcan, the only two SNc clusters that express Anxa1.
source: Of note, the highest scDRS scores were in clusters Sox6Tafa1 and Sox6Vcan, the only two SNc clusters that express Anxa1.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the scDRS analysis.

claim: Only the Sox6 family (and Anxa1-expressing SNc clusters within it) show significant associations with PD risk loci at a population level.
source: By calculating the average scores for each cluster family as a whole, as well as these two Anxa1-expressing SNc clusters, we found that only the Sox6 family (and Anxa1-expressing SNc clusters within it) show significant associations with PD risk loci at a population level (Figure 9H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9H.

claim: The study provides a large snRNA-seq dataset that provides high granularity to taxonomic schemes of DA neurons.
source: Our work provides five key advances. 1. We provide a large snRNA-seq dataset that provides high granularity to our taxonomic schemes.
evidence: This is stated as a key advance in the discussion.

claim: The study provides a user-friendly portal to query the dataset.
source: Our work provides five key advances. 1. We provide a large snRNA-seq dataset that provides high granularity to our taxonomic schemes. 2. We provide a user-friendly portal to query this dataset.
evidence: This is stated as a key advance in the discussion.

claim: The study plots the spatial location of most identified DA neuron subtypes, showing heterogeneity even within sub-domains in traditional anatomical areas.
source: 3. We plot the spatial location of most identified DA neuron subtypes, showing heterogeneity even within sub-domains in traditional anatomical areas.
evidence: This is stated as a key advance in the discussion.

claim: Cluster proportions do not change in LRRK2G2019S mice, although gene expression changes are observed, most notably in mitochondrial bioenergetics and synapse organization pathways in vulnerable DA subtypes.
source: 4. We demonstrate that cluster proportions do not change in LRRK2G2019S mice, although gene expression changes are observed, most notably in mitochondrial bioenergetics and synapse organization pathways in vulnerable DA subtypes.
evidence: This is stated as a key advance in the discussion.

claim: PD GWAS risk is most prominent in Anxa1 SNc neurons.
source: 5. PD GWAS risk is most prominent in Anxa1 SNc neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a key advance in the discussion.

claim: The study demonstrates the presence of 20 molecularly distinct clusters of midbrain DA neurons that are hierarchically organized.
source: We demonstrate the presence of 20 molecularly distinct clusters of midbrain DA neurons. These are hierarchically organized, the dendrogram being split into three levels, which we refer to as family, branch, and subtype.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding in the discussion.

claim: Family (Level 1) distinctions are driven by the expression of Gad2/Kctd16 vs Slc6a3/Ddc high expressing cells.
source: Family (Level 1) distinctions are driven by the expression of Gad2/Kctd16 vs Slc6a3/Ddc high expressing cells.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the hierarchical organization.

claim: Slc6a3/Ddc high cells are further divided by Sox6/Col25a1 and Calb1/Ndst3 (Level 2).
source: Slc6a3/Ddc high cells are further divided by Sox6/Col25a1 and Calb1/Ndst3 (Level 2) among other genes.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the hierarchical organization.

claim: The fundamental divisions between Sox6 and Calb1 are likely set early in development in the mesodiencephalic floor plate.
source: It is likely that these fundamental divisions are, at least in part, set early in development in the mesodiencephalic floor plate, where Sox6 demarcates progenitors with a substantially higher probability of ventral SNc and lateral VTA fate, and conversely, Sox6- progenitors have a higher probability of a Calb1+ fate (Pereira Luppi et al., 2021; Panman et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation with citations to prior literature.

claim: This taxonomic scheme represents a more granular taxonomy than previous studies.
source: This scheme represents a more granular taxonomy than previous studies (La Manno et al., 2016; Kramer et al., 2018; Hook et al., 2018; Saunders et al., 2018; Azcorra et al., 2023; Poulin et al., 2014; Kamath et al., 2022), and bears some resemblance to a recent study (Yaghmaeian Salmani et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to prior literature.

claim: The spatial MERFISH analysis provides the most granular representation of DA subtype locations to date.
source: Our spatial MERFISH analysis provides the most granular representation of DA subtype locations to date.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding in the discussion.

claim: A key finding of this study is the heterogeneity observed even within sub-domains of the traditional anatomical clusters.
source: A key finding of this study is the heterogeneity observed even within sub-domains of the traditional anatomical clusters.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding in the discussion.

claim: Secondary gene expression programs may have been superimposed upon the early developmental sub-divisions, for instance during circuit assembly.
source: One interpretation of this is that secondary gene expression programs may have been superimposed upon the early developmental sub-divisions, for instance during circuit assembly.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observed heterogeneity.

claim: A strength of the study is that it utilizes advantages of each transcriptomic approach, the deep molecular profiling of individual cells using snRNA-seq and the spatial resolution of MERFISH.
source: A strength of our study is that it utilizes advantages of each transcriptomic approach, the deep molecular profiling of individual cells using snRNA-seq and the spatial resolution of MERFISH.
evidence: This is stated as a strength of the study in the discussion.

claim: Gene imputation as described by Stuart et al., 2019 has been used in several recent studies integrating spatial and transcriptomic data.
source: Gene imputation as described by Stuart et al., 2019 has been used in several recent studies integrating spatial and transcriptomic data (Zhang et al., 2023; Yao et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: Imputed Sox6 expression accurately reflects what has been reported in prior immunofluorescence and in situ hybridization studies.
source: This approach was used to impute Sox6 expression, which accurately reflects what has been reported in prior immunofluorescence and in situ hybridization studies (Avvisati et al., 2024; Poulin et al., 2018; Poulin et al., 2014; Pereira Luppi et al., 2021; Panman et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: The proportions of subtypes are largely consistent between controls and mutants, and mutant subtypes are most closely related to their control counterpart.
source: We show that the proportions of subtypes are largely consistent between controls and mutants, and that mutant subtypes are most closely related to their control counterpart.
evidence: This is stated as evidence that the clustering scheme reflects cell types rather than cell states.

claim: The taxonomic scheme is agnostic to a mild perturbation such as LRRK2G2019S, suggesting that the clusters are reflective of cell types, rather than cell states.
source: This suggests that our taxonomic scheme is agnostic to a mild perturbation such as LRRK2G2019S, suggesting that our clusters are reflective of cell types, rather than cell states.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the stability of cluster proportions.

claim: With more severe perturbations, such as a toxin lesion, more substantial alterations of taxonomic schemes may be observed.
source: It is possible that with more severe perturbations, such as a toxin lesion, more substantial alterations of taxonomic schemes are observed (Yaghmaeian Salmani et al., 2024; Tang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as speculation with citations to prior literature.

claim: The work describes a rich heterogeneity of DA neurons in the murine SNc that might serve as a reference for understanding patterns of degeneration in PD.
source: Our work describes a rich heterogeneity of DA neurons in the murine SNc that might serve as a reference for understanding patterns of degeneration in PD.
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of the findings.

claim: Several studies on post-mortem human PD brain have demonstrated a relative resilience of Calb1+ DA neurons.
source: Several studies on post-mortem human PD brain have demonstrated a relative resilience of Calb1 + DA neurons (Pereira Luppi et al., 2021; Yamada et al., 1990; Damier et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: Calb1+ neurons in mice SNc and SNpl project most densely to the dorsomedial striatum (DMS) and tail of striatum (TS), respectively.
source: Calb1 + neurons in mice SNc and SNpl project most densely to the dorsomedial striatum (DMS) and tail of striatum (TS), respectively (Gaertner et al., 2022; Poulin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: Patterns of axon preservation observed in post-mortem PD brain show relative sparing of medial, ventral, and caudal regions of the caudate-putamen.
source: This could match the patterns of axon preservation observed in post-mortem PD brain, which show relative sparing of medial, ventral, and caudal regions of the caudate-putamen (Kish et al., 1988; Kordower et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: It is plausible that patterns of degeneration could be associated with distinct clinical presentations of PD.
source: Indeed it is plausible that patterns of degeneration could be associated with distinct clinical presentations of PD – a recent study suggests that patients with relatively spared caudate projections have a higher probability of tremor (Mendonça et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated as speculation with citation to a recent study.

claim: Spared DA neuron projections may be a cellular substrate mediating the side-effects of levodopa particularly at high doses.
source: Additionally, we postulate that spared DA neurons projections may be a cellular substrate mediating the side-effects of levodopa particularly at high doses.
evidence: This is stated as speculation.

claim: High DA release in the TS is associated with hallucination-like behaviors in mice.
source: In line with this, high DA release in the TS is associated with hallucination-like behaviors in mice (Schmack et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citation to prior literature.

claim: The study relied on a KI LRRK2 model expressing the G2019S pathogenic mutation due to the highest prevalence of this mutation over other mutations.
source: We relied on a KI LRRK2 model, expressing the G2019S pathogenic mutation due to the highest prevalence of this mutation over other mutations.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological choice.

claim: LRRK2G2019S KI mice do not exhibit DA neuron loss but have nigrostriatal synaptic alterations within a physiological range.
source: Although these mice do not exhibit DA neuron loss, they do have nigrostriatal synaptic alterations within a physiological range (Xenias et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated with citation to prior literature.

claim: Transcriptomic alterations observed within DA neurons are potentially cell-autonomous effects of LRRK2G2019S.
source: Thus, transcriptomic alterations observed within DA neurons are potentially cell-autonomous effects, albeit indirect, since LRRK2 functions as a protein kinase with phosphoregulation primarily affected.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Pathway analysis showed a strong dysregulation of synaptic pathways in LRRK2G2019S mutants.
source: Second, while individual genes showed only modest differences, pathway analysis showed a strong dysregulation of synaptic pathways.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding from the pathway analysis.

claim: LRRK2 phosphorylates various key presynaptic targets associated with SV cycle.
source: This is conceptually aligned with prior work describing that LRRK2 phosphorylates various key presynaptic targets (not necessarily in DA axons) associated with SV cycle (Pischedda and Piccoli, 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citation to prior literature.

claim: Impairments of presynaptic processes at the nigrostriatal terminals may contribute to the DA release deficits reported in LRRK2 mutants.
source: Impairments of these processes at the nigrostriatal terminals may contribute to the DA release deficits reported in LRRK2 mutants (Xenias et al., 2022; Yue et al., 2015; Tozzi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation connecting the findings to prior reports.

claim: Alterations in pathways associated with oxidative phosphorylation and energy production are in line with the described LRRK2 impact on mitochondrial structure and mitophagy in the LRRK2G2019S KI mice.
source: Third, alterations in pathways associated with oxidative phosphorylation and energy production are in line with the described LRRK2 impact on mitochondrial structure and mitophagy in the LRRK2G2019S KI mice.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation connecting the findings to prior knowledge.

claim: DA transmission changes and mitochondrial abnormalities are the two main and consistent phenotypes with the KI mouse model.
source: As DA transmission changes and mitochondrial abnormalities are the two main and consistent phenotypes with the KI mouse model, our transcriptomic findings indicate that functional changes are at least partly linked with gene expression changes.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the findings.

claim: The work complements the recent taxonomy of mouse and human brain cell types.
source: Taken together, our work complements perfectly the recent taxonomy of mouse (Zhang et al., 2023; Yao et al., 2023; Langlieb et al., 2023; Yaghmaeian Salmani et al., 2024) and human brain cell types (Siletti et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to recent literature.

claim: The study provides a web resource to explore the dataset through multiple angles.
source: Moreover, we provide a web resource to explore this dataset through multiple angles.
evidence: This is stated as a contribution of the study.

claim: The study uncovered cell type-specific transcriptomic changes in a prodromal model of PD revealing the molecular consequences of higher LRRK2 activity.
source: We also uncovered cell type-specific transcriptomic changes in a prodromal model of PD revealing the molecular consequences of higher LRRK2 activity.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding of the study.

claim: By defining genetic anchor points unique to each subtype, the study has provided an avenue to target these populations in the mouse.
source: Decades of experiments might be needed to answer such questions, however, by defining genetic anchor points unique to each subtype, we have provided an avenue to target these populations in the mouse.
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of the findings.
